ops.description:
Found by the Phase-0 invariant census, **verified independently at `origin/main` = `1d55b2a`** before filing. **Amended twice since — the comments carry the corrections; the Q7 measurement (2026-07-28) overturned both the mechanism and the exposure originally stated here. This body is the amended version.**

## The defect

`rejectInjectionEntitlements` exists in exactly one of the two peer-verification implementations:

```
ccx code grep "rejectInjectionEntitlements"
# 2 matches in 1 files
### trust/verify_darwin.go:328,334
```

`codeidentity/verify_darwin.go` has **zero matches**. So `codeidentity` accepts a peer signed with injection-enabling entitlements which `trust` rejects.

## Mechanism — corrected by Q7

`deployment` does **not** verify through `codeidentity`. It uses the package as a value type (`CodeIdentity`, `PolicyDigest`) and verifies via its own `c.verifier`. The **single production call site** of `codeidentity`'s verifier is `service/keepalive.go:420`.

Q7 also measured the real gap: **two entitlements, not four.** `allow-jit` and `allow-dyld-environment-variables` leave dynamic csflags bit-identical to a clean hardened-runtime binary — no status-word check can close them. `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` and `disable-executable-page-protection` **do** clear `CS_ENFORCEMENT`/`CS_HARD`, which `codeidentity` checks neither of — closable literal-free. The "stronger on library validation" difference (first comment) is code-true but **verdict-false**: no constructible peer that `codeidentity` rejects and `trust` accepts.

## Why it happened — the pattern, not the instance

This is the second confirmed instance of *the same* failure mode. Commit `d09ed52` (the `ErrPeerGone` classification fix) had to apply the identical change to **both** copies to be correct. A fix landing in one copy and not the other is the structural hazard, and there is no compile-time or CI signal for it.

**Do not fix this by copying the function.** A same-fix-twice patch closes this instance and preserves the generator — and it is mechanically blocked anyway: entitlement-string literals in package `codeidentity` embed signed-only policy into every daemon-facing binary and turn an existing (load-bearing) test red.

## Interim exposure — corrected

Until resolved, a binary signed with `allow-jit` (or either csflags-clearing entitlement) passes `codeidentity` verification at `service/keepalive.go:420` — the keepalive verify path. Deployment's install path never consults this verifier.

## Resolution (scheduled, remediation Phase 1)

P1-a lands the literal-free half now (`CS_ENFORCEMENT|CS_HARD` requirement in codeidentity + the trust absence-fixture fix). P1-f (fable) designs the `trust.ProcessVerifier` inversion — child owns policy, parent sends `CodeIdentity` + expected `PolicyDigest`. P1-g deletes `codeidentity`'s verifier and repoints keepalive, gated by a sol finder+refuter security review. Value types and the 3 sentinels survive.
